stem: A child with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is being reviewed before ENT surgery. Which finding most directly supports avoiding adenoidectomy in this syndrome?

options.text: Velopharyngeal insufficiency related to palate anomalies
A high risk of postoperative iron deficiency
Generalised muscle weakness from elevated creatine kinase

explanation: Velopharyngeal insufficiency related to palate anomalies is the correct answer. In 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, palate abnormalities can make adenoidectomy worsen speech resonance by reducing velopharyngeal closure.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome (Velocardiofacial Syndrome +/- Di George Syndrome)

rationale: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome can include palate anomalies that predispose to velopharyngeal insufficiency, so adenoidectomy may be avoided to prevent worsening speech problems.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because palate anomalies in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome can cause velopharyngeal insufficiency, and adenoidectomy may worsen this.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because iron deficiency is not the surgical consideration that supports avoiding adenoidectomy in this syndrome.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because nephrotic syndrome relapse is not the relevant feature of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because progressive long-bone fractures are not the key ENT-related issue in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because elevated creatine kinase with muscle weakness is not the finding that explains avoiding adenoidectomy in this syndrome.
